newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union may widen truck strike to rail, air.
newsitem.headline: French union may widen truck strike to rail, air.

text.p: France's Workers Force (FO) trade union threatened on Monday to widen a week-old truck drivers' strike blocking highways and borders to rail and air transport if negotiators did not reach a deal by Tuesday.

FO leader Marc Blondel told reporters after meeting Transport Minister Bernard Pons: "What I can say very clearly is that if there is not a result by tomorrow morning, Workers Force will examine the conditions for extending the movement to (public) transport."
He was speaking after trade unions and employers began another night of talks chaired by a government mediator on the truckers' demands for better pay, shorter working hours and earlier retirement.

"Tonight's negotiation is decisive," said Blondel, whose union is the third largest among truckers and rail workers. "Solidarity can be expressed in different ways, for example by launching a strike at the SNCF (state railway) and in civil aviation too. Bringing all forms of transport out in solidarity with the truckers would be a first step."
Striking truck drivers increased the number of blockades on motorways, around fuel depots and at borders to 180 by Monday evening from 136 earlier in the day, union officials said.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe called earlier for a resumption and conclusion of the talks, saying the government was doing all it could to facilitate a deal.
